The '''2014 FA Community Shield''' (also known as '''The FA Community Shield supported by [[McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 92nd [[FA Community Shield]], an annual English [[association football|football]] match played between the winners of the previous season's [[Premier League]] and [[FA Cup]]. The game was played between [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who beat [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in the [[2014 FA Cup final|final]] of the [[2013–14 FA Cup]], and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], champions of the [[2013–14 Premier League]].

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] were the holders, having won the [[2013 FA Community Shield|2013 edition]], but did not qualify for this match, as they finished seventh in the [[2013–14 Premier League|Premier League]] and were knocked out of the [[2013–14 FA Cup|FA Cup]] in the third round.

This was Arsenal's 20th Community Shield appearance and Manchester City's 10th. The only time the two teams previously met in the Shield was in [[1934 FA Charity Shield|1934]], when Arsenal won 4&ndash;0. The 2014 staging of the event was the first to use [[vanishing spray]], following its success at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]]. In the lead up to the match Manchester City manager [[Manuel Pellegrini]] defended his club's transfer recruitment, after it was questioned by the Arsenal manager [[Arsène Wenger]].

[[Alexis Sánchez]] was one of three players who made their competitive debuts for Arsenal in the match; for Manchester City, goalkeeper [[Willy Caballero]] was selected ahead of [[Joe Hart]]. Arsenal began the game more strongly and took the lead when [[Santi Cazorla]] scored in the 22nd minute. Their lead was extended two minutes before half time, as [[Aaron Ramsey]] finished off a counter-attacking move. Arsenal scored their third of the match soon after the hour mark; [[Olivier Giroud]]'s shot from outside the penalty box dipped over Caballero and into his goal.

Watched by a crowd of 71,523 at [[Wembley Stadium]] in London, Arsenal won the match 3–0. It was the biggest win at the Community Shield in [[1998 FA Charity Shield|16 years]], when they defeated United, City's [[Manchester derby|cross-city rivals]]. Wenger was pleased with his team's performance and felt the win would provide a confidence boost for the coming season. Pellegrini's reaction was indifferent; he believed the absence of several first team players was linked to their poor show.

==Background==
Founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=19 April 1908}}</ref> the [[FA Community Shield]] began as a contest between the respective champions of the [[English Football League|Football League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], although in 1913 it was played between an Amateurs XI and a Professionals XI.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=[[The Times]] |location=London |date=7 October 1913}}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the league champions of the top division and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Peter |last=Ferguson |title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |website=mcfc.co.uk |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=8 August 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192421/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |url-status=dead }}</ref>{{#tag:ref|The [[Premier League]] replaced the [[Football League First Division]] at the top of the [[English football league system|English football pyramid]] after its inception in 1992.<ref>{{cite news |title=Continental or the full English? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/dec/02/sport.sportfeatures |first=Alex |last=Fynn |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=2 December 2001 |access-date=8 August 2014}}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} As part of a sponsorship deal between [[The Football Association]] and American restaurant chain [[McDonald's]], the match was officially referred to as "The FA Community Shield supported by McDonald's".<ref>{{cite web |title=Wembley to welcome troops to Community Shield |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/thefa/2014/aug/wembley-to-welcome-hundreds-of-the-armed-forces-to-community-shield-070814 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=7 August 2014 |access-date=8 August 2014}}</ref>

[[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] qualified for the 2014 FA Community Shield as winners of the [[2013–14 Premier League]]. The club saw off competition from [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and won their second league title in three years with victory against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on the last day.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester City crowned champions after effortless win over West Ham |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/may/11/manchester-city-west-ham-premier-league-match-report |first=Daniel |last=Taylor |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=11 May 2014 |access-date=8 August 2014}}</ref> The other Community Shield place went to Arsenal, who defeated [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in extra time to win the [[2014 FA Cup final|final]] of the [[2013–14 FA Cup]]. It ended a run of nine years without a trophy for the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arséne Wenger savours FA Cup win over Hull as Arsenal end drought |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/may/18/arsene-wenger-fa-cup-arsenal-hull-trophy-drought|first=David |last=Hytner |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=18 May 2014 |access-date=8 August 2014}}</ref>

Manchester City made their 10th Community Shield appearance; prior to this, they won four ([[1937 FA Charity Shield|1937]], [[1968 FA Charity Shield|1968]], [[1972 FA Charity Shield|1972]], [[2012 FA Community Shield|2012]]) and lost five – one of which against Arsenal in [[1934 FA Charity Shield|1934]]. By contrast, Arsenal made their 20th Community Shield appearance, a record bettered only by [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] (29) and Liverpool (21). Arsenal had won 12 times, 11 of which were won outright, most recently in [[2004 FA Community Shield|2004]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |title=England – List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |date=15 August 2013 |access-date=8 August 2014 |first=James |last=Ross |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305035734/http://rsssf.com/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |archive-date=5 March 2016 |df=dmy }}</ref>

The match was televised live in the United Kingdom on [[BT Sport]];<ref>{{cite news |title=BT Sport to screen Community Shield |url=http://sport.bt.com/sportfootball/football/bt-sport-to-screen-community-shield-S11363912261292 |publisher=BT Sport |date=17 June 2014 |access-date=8 August 2014}}</ref> the network obtained rights to the Community Shield in July 2013 as part of a four-year deal with the [[BBC]] to air live [[FA Cup]] football.<ref>{{cite news |title=FA confirms new TV deals |url=http://www.thefa.com/News/2013/jul/bt-sport-bbc-itv-2014-18.aspx |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=17 July 2013 |access-date=8 August 2014}}</ref>

==Build-up==
Arsenal manager [[Arsène Wenger]] used his press conference before the match to look ahead to the new season. He wanted his team to build on their FA Cup success and said that the Community Shield "...will be the best way to prepare for the start of the League season next week."<ref>{{cite news |title=Wenger eyes a positive start in Community Shield |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/competitions/fa-community-shield/2014/aug/arsene-wenger-community-shield-preview |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=9 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref> Wenger was surprised his opponents Manchester City had taken midfielder [[Frank Lampard]] from their own franchise club [[New York City FC]] on loan; he questioned whether this was a way to bypass [[UEFA]]'s [[Financial Fair Play]] rules.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester City midfielder Frank Lampard is no traitor – Chelsea didn't want him any more, says Manuel Pellegrini |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-city/11021609/Manchester-City-midfielder-Frank-Lampard-is-no-traitor-Chelsea-didnt-want-him-any-more-says-Manuel-Pellegrini.html |first=Tim |last=Abraham |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=8 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref> Of [[Bacary Sagna]]'s move from Arsenal to Manchester City in the summer, Wenger told reporters: "I made him a proposal to stay for three years, but he chose them. Had he chosen a long time ago? Maybe – it looks to me like he agreed it a long time before."<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal's Wenger 'surprised and disappointed' as title rivals Man City add Lampard and Sagna |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/arsenals-wenger-surprised-disappointed-title-4021746#.U-i5nKP1olp |first=Mike |last=Walters |newspaper=Daily Mirror |location=London |date=7 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref> Wenger also revealed Arsenal had received offers for defender [[Thomas Vermaelen]];<ref>{{cite news |title=Thomas Vermaelen: Arsenal boss Wenger drops Man Utd hint |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28685189 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=7 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref> on the day of the Community Shield match the player transferred to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Thomas Vermaelen: Barcelona seal move for Arsenal defender |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28728256 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref>
[[File:Manuel Pellegrini 2013.jpg|thumb|175px|[[Manuel Pellegrini]] said that Manchester City would use the Community Shield as a way to start the season well.]] 
[[Manuel Pellegrini]], the manager of Manchester City, said before the game that winning the Shield "would be the ideal start to the campaign."<ref name="pelb">{{cite news |title=Pellegrini: Community Shield win would be 'ideal'|url=http://www.thefa.com/news/competitions/fa-community-shield/2014/aug/manuel-pellegrini-community-shield-preview |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=7 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref> He was conscious of his team's poor start to the previous season and wanted them to do better, particularly away from home.<ref name="pelb"/> Pellegrini did not see the game against Arsenal as a "[[Exhibition game|friendly]]", and expected his opponents to provide a good test for Manchester City in the Shield match and thereafter in the league season.<ref name="pelb"/><ref name="pelli">{{cite news |title=It's no friendly, says Pellegrini as he faces old foe Wenger |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/community-shield-its-no-friendly-says-pellegrini-as-he-faces-old-foe-wenger-9658710.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/community-shield-its-no-friendly-says-pellegrini-as-he-faces-old-foe-wenger-9658710.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |first=Tim |last=Rich |newspaper=The Independent |publisher=London |date=9 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He was satisfied overall with the club's transfer activity during the summer, in particular praising goalkeeper [[Willy Caballero]].<ref name="buid">{{cite news |title=City v Arsenal: Community Shield preview |url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/manchester-city-v-arsenal-fc-7587905 |first=David |last=Lynch |newspaper=Manchester Evening News |date=9 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref> When asked about Wenger's comments about Manchester City, he retorted: "As a manager we have enough problems with our own teams to be talking about other teams."<ref name="pelli"/> Pellegrini expressed his belief that Lampard's transfer was not done by underhand tactics – "we didn’t spend any money in bringing him from New York City to Manchester City," and added the player was not offered a contract to remain at [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Manuel Pellegrini happy Manchester City dealt with transfers properly |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11679/9412641/premier-league-manuel-pellegrini-happy-manchester-city-dealt-with-transfers-properly |publisher=Sky Sports |date=8 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref>

[[Aaron Ramsey]], who scored Arsenal's winning goal in the FA Cup final, was adamant their recent success would make his teammates determined to win more. He aimed for victory in the Community Shield, as it would provide a platform for what he described as "a tough opening couple of games in the Premier League."<ref>{{cite news |first=Gary |last=Stonehouse |title=Ramsey wants another Wembley day to remember |url=http://www.thefa.com/News/competitions/fa-community-shield/2014/aug/aaron-ramsey-community-shield-preview |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=7 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref> [[Samir Nasri]], who left Arsenal to join Manchester City in 2011, in the lead-up to the match described the abuse he received from Arsenal supporters since his transfer as "stupid." He went on to explain: "They see it as treason or that I betrayed them but it’s not like that. I just look what’s best for me ... For the fans the only reason [to leave] has to be for the money. But it isn’t just for the money."<ref>{{cite news |title=Samir Nasri ready to make the best moves for himself and Manchester City |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/aug/09/samir-nasri-manchester-city-community-shield-arsenal-france |first=Andy |last=Hunter |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=9 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref>

Both clubs received an allocation of approximately 26,000 tickets.<ref name="prs">{{cite news |title=Community Shield details announced |url=http://www.wembleystadium.com/Press/Press-Releases/2014/6/Community-Shield-Announce |publisher=Wembley Stadium |date=17 June 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref> Manchester City fans were housed in the east end of Wembley, while Arsenal fans occupied the west.<ref>{{cite news |title=The FA Community Shield Supporter Information 2014 |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/~/media/Files/The%20FA%20Community%20Shield%20Supporter%20Information%202014.ashx |website=mcfc.co.uk |publisher=Manchester City FC |format=PDF |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014 |archive-date=12 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812203520/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/~/media/Files/The%20FA%20Community%20Shield%20Supporter%20Information%202014.ashx |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Information for Community Shield |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20140808/information-for-community-shield |publisher=Arsenal Football Club |date=8 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref> Ticket prices stayed the same for the third consecutive year and were advertised at a cost of between £20 and £45; the tickets went on general sale for Manchester City fans on 22 July 2014.<ref name="prs"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Community Shield: Ticket information |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/tickets-and-travel/2014/july/community-shield-ticket-news |website=mcfc.co.uk |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=21 July 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014 |archive-date=12 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812031147/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/tickets-and-travel/2014/july/community-shield-ticket-news |url-status=dead }}</ref> Arsenal chief executive [[Ivan Gazidis]] was upset by the low allocation: "We have expressed our disappointment to the FA regarding the ticket allocation for both the FA Cup final and FA Community Shield."<ref>{{cite news |title=Ticket details for FA Community Shield |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20140630/ticket-details-for-fa-community-shield |publisher=Arsenal Football Club |date=30 June 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref>

[[Michael Oliver (referee)|Michael Oliver]] was selected as the referee for the Shield match; it marked the fifth time he refereed at Wembley Stadium.<ref name="officials">{{cite web |title=Michael Oliver to referee FA Community Shield |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/competitions/fa-community-shield/2014/jul/michael-oliver-appointed-shield-referee-010714 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=1 July 2014 |access-date=22 July 2014 }}</ref> The game was the first in English football to use [[vanishing spray]], designed to help referees mark free-kick positions. This came after the spray's success at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Community shield: Vanishing spray to make English debut |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28689542 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=7 August 2014 |access-date=13 August 2014}}</ref> English rock band [[Embrace (English band)|Embrace]] provided pre-match entertainment and ''[[Britain's Got Talent]]'' finalist [[List of Britain's Got Talent finalists (series 8)#Lucy Kay|Lucy Kay]] sung the national anthem before the match commenced.<ref>{{cite news |title=Community Shield acts confirmed for Wembley |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/competitions/fa-community-shield/2014/aug/embrace-and-lucy-kay-to-perform-at-community-shield-050814 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=5 August 2014 |access-date=12 August 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Lucy Kay sings the national anthem during the FA Community Shield |url=http://www.gettyimages.co.uk/detail/news-photo/lucy-kay-sings-the-national-anthem-during-the-fa-community-news-photo/453484924 |publisher=Getty Images |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=12 August 2014 }}</ref>

==Match==

===Team selection===
[[File:Community Shield 14 - Managers lead the teams out (14698393168).jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.15|The two teams led out by their managers]]
Manchester City were predicted to line up in a [[Formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–2–3–1]] formation, with Nasri and [[James Milner]] as wide men.<ref name="form">{{cite news |title=Arsenal v Manchester City |page=S4 |newspaper=The Sunday Telegraph |location=London |date=11 August 2014}}</ref> Due to a specified pre-season programme, Pellegrini had agreed to excuse several players from the match, namely [[Martín Demichelis]], [[Vincent Kompany]], [[Pablo Zabaleta]], [[Bacary Sagna]], [[Fernandinho (footballer, born May 1985)|Fernandinho]], [[Frank Lampard]] and [[Sergio Agüero]]. Striker [[Álvaro Negredo]] was also unavailable for selection because of an injury.<ref name="buid"/> Arsenal were expected to line up similarly to Manchester City, with Ramsey as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|holding midfielder]], and [[Tomáš Rosický]] in an advanced role behind [[Olivier Giroud]].<ref name="form"/> Goalkeeper [[David Ospina]] was ruled out of the game with a thigh injury; German internationals [[Per Mertesacker]], [[Mesut Özil]] and [[Lukas Podolski]] did not feature as they were given extended time off following their national side's success at the World Cup.<ref name="buid"/>

When the teamsheets were released, Wenger's selection showed Rosický and Giroud would start the match as substitutes and competitive debuts were given to [[Mathieu Debuchy]], [[Calum Chambers]] and [[Alexis Sánchez]]. Arsenal employed a [[Formation (association football)#4–1–4–1|4–1–4–1]] formation to start the game, with a defensive midfielder ([[Mikel Arteta]]) sitting between a flat back four and a four-man midfield; [[Yaya Sanogo]] led the Arsenal attack as a lone [[Forward (association football)#Centre forward|centre-forward]].<ref name="wemb">{{cite news |title=The FA Community Shield |url=http://www.wembleystadium.com/Events/2014/Community-Shield/Community-Shield |publisher=Wembley Stadium |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref>

Manchester City organised themselves slightly differently, with two defensive midfielders and an attacking midfielder – [[Stevan Jovetić]] &ndash; playing behind the main striker, [[Edin Džeko]]. Caballero and [[Fernando (footballer, born 1987)|Fernando]] made their debuts for the club, while [[Bruno Zuculini]] was named on the bench. The team lined up in a [[Formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–2–3–1]] formation.<ref name="wemb"/> There were no English players in the Manchester City starting XI.<ref name=engl>{{cite news |title=Pellegrini not worried over English influence |url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/pellegrini-not-worried-over-english-7594672 |first=David |last=Lynch |newspaper=Manchester Evening News |date=11 August 2014 |access-date=13 August 2014}}</ref>

===Summary===

====First half====
[[File:Community Shield Nasri corner.jpg|thumb|Samir Nasri taking a corner in the first half]]
Manchester City got the match underway and won the first [[corner kick]] of the match in the fifth minute.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Sanghera|first1=Mandeep|title=Arsenal 3–0 Man City |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28647186|access-date=8 January 2015|publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=10 August 2014}}</ref> In the eighth minute, Debuchy crossed the ball from the right, but Sanogo's attempt to head the ball was impeded by Clichy.<ref name="telec">{{cite news |title=Community Shield: Arsenal v Manchester City |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-city/11024269/Arsenal-v-Manchester-City-live.html |first=Alan |last=Tyers |work=Telegraph.co.uk |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}}</ref>  An Arsenal corner minutes after resulted in Manchester City reacting with a counter-attack; the ball eventually reached an unmarked Nasri in the penalty area, but the midfielder's shot on goal was blocked by Debuchy's arm.<ref name="guardr">{{cite news |title=Arsenal win Community Shield with victory over Manchester City – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2014/aug/10/arsenal-manchester-city-community-shield-live-wembley-mbm |first=Michael |last=Butler |work=theguardian.com |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}}</ref> Manchester City appealed for a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]], which was not given by referee Oliver. Arsenal continued to build pressure in Manchester City's half and scored the opening goal. Sanogo kept possession of the ball and passed to Wilshere, who was tackled. The ball then fell to [[Santi Cazorla]], who created space for himself and shot into the bottom right hand corner of Caballero's goal.<ref name="guardr"/> A corner taken by Nasri in the 22nd minute was greeted by jeers from the Arsenal supporters, as was his every touch of the ball.<ref name="telec"/> Near the half-hour mark Arsenal countered through Sánchez, but his pass to Ramsey was quickly intercepted. From a corner, Sanogo directed his header straight at Caballero.<ref name="skyc">{{cite news |title=Live Commentary |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/319570/commentary |publisher=Sky Sports |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}}</ref> As the game went on Manchester City began to gather momentum, with [[Aleksandar Kolarov]] finding success from attacking Arsenal's right.<ref name="guardr"/> Despite improved play, Manchester City were losing 0&ndash;2 after 42 minutes when Sanogo began the move by keeping possession and finding Ramsey with a pass. The midfielder took one touch to side-step [[Matija Nastasić]] and another to put the ball into the net.<ref name="skyc"/> Arsenal came close to scoring a third goal just before half-time when Sanogo and Sánchez exchanged passes near the Manchester City area, but Caballero came out of his penalty box to break up the move.<ref name="telec"/>

====Second half====
[[File:Community Shield 31 - Celebrating Giroud's goal (14862008386).jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.15|The Arsenal players celebrating Olivier Giroud's goal.]]
Arsenal made a triple substitution before the second half commenced – [[Laurent Koscielny]], Sánchez and Sanogo came off for [[Nacho Monreal]], [[Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain]] and Olivier Giroud.<ref name="guardr"/> Manchester City meanwhile replaced Nasri with [[David Silva]].<ref name="guardr"/> In contrast to the first 45 minutes, Manchester City started well; three minutes after the start of the half, Kolarov collected the ball from Silva and charged forward, but his cross on the left flank was cleared by Monreal.<ref name="guardr"/> In the 50th minute, Fernando was shown the game's first and only yellow card for fouling Wilshere.<ref name="telec"/> Manchester City continued to fashion opportunities: Navas beat his opponent [[Kieran Gibbs]] on the right and crossed the ball in the Arsenal area. Jovetić's header was kept out by [[Wojciech Szczęsny]] and on the rebound he struck the ball over the goal.<ref name="skyc"/> Szczęsny denied Jovetić again in the 56th minute, diving to his right to clear.<ref name="skyc"/> Manchester City made two changes on the hour, bringing on Milner and [[Bruno Zuculini]] for Džeko and [[Yaya Touré]].<ref name="guardr"/> A shot by Giroud from {{convert|25|yd}} dipped over Caballero and landed in the net to make it 3&ndash;0 to Arsenal. Manchester City responded with some opportunities to score – Jovetić's attempt at an overhead kick went over the bar in the 65th minute, and minutes later Szczęsny saved from Zuculini in a collision which required treatment for both players.<ref name="skyc"/> Both teams made more substitutions in the final third of the game – for Arsenal [[Mathieu Flamini]], Rosický and debutant [[Joel Campbell]] replaced Wilshere, Cazorla and Ramsey respectively, while Manchester City brought on [[Micah Richards]] and [[Scott Sinclair]] in place of Kolarov and Navas.<ref name="guardr"/> Near the end, Szczęsny came out of his penalty box and cleared the ball with his head, but inadvertently collided with Sinclair.<ref name="repo">{{cite news |title=Community Shield: Arsenal v Manchester City |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/28731476 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810125128/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/28731476 |url-status=dead |archive-date=10 August 2014 |first=Tom |last=Rostance |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref>

===Details===
{{football box
|date=10 August 2014
|time=15:00 [[British Summer Time|BST]]
|team1=[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]
|score=3–0

==Post-match==
{{Quote box |width=260px |bgcolor=#FFFFF0 |salign=left |quote="I repeat this was a special game but during the year I don’t look at the nationality of the players. I use the players I think are the best players to win that game. It doesn’t matter where they come from."|source=[[Manuel Pellegrini]] on his non-English starting XI.<ref name=engl/>}}
The trophy was presented to Arteta by former Arsenal player and assistant coach [[Pat Rice]].<ref name="repo"/> Arsenal's win marked the biggest victory in the Community Shield since [[1998 FA Charity Shield|1998]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal first FA Cup winners in five years to win Community Shield |url=http://infostradalive.com/2014/08/10/review-arsenal-first-fa-cup-winners-in-five-years-to-win-community-shield/ |publisher=Infostrada Live |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140818210253/http://infostradalive.com/2014/08/10/review-arsenal-first-fa-cup-winners-in-five-years-to-win-community-shield/ |archive-date=18 August 2014 |url-status=usurped |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Wenger was delighted with his team's performance and described their play in the first half as complete. He noted that although Arsenal lost possession in the second half and looked "less fluent", the team retained "spirit and organisation".<ref>{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Hall |title=Arsene Wenger buoyant after 'complete performance' |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/competitions/fa-community-shield/2014/aug/arsene-wenger-buoyant-after-community-shield-win |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014 }}</ref> He described the win as significant because it gave Arsenal a confidence boost going into the season and suggested it was important to beat a top-six league team because of their poor record last season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsène Wenger buoyant after Arsenal's convincing win over Manchester City |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/aug/10/arsene-wenger-arsenal-manchester-city-community-shield |first=Sachin |last=Nakrani |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref> Wenger was happy with how Arsenal's new signings came through the match and reserved special praise for Chambers: "He played with a maturity and intelligence that I was really impressed with."<ref>{{cite news |title=Boss on Chambers and another trophy |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20140810/boss-on-chambers-and-another-trophy |first=Chris |last=Harris |publisher=Arsenal Football Club |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref> [[Olivier Giroud]], the [[man of the match]], said of his goal: "I tried instinctively to shoot and to hit the target. I was a bit lucky but that's what I wanted to do."<ref>{{cite news |title=Giroud on his Community Shield goal |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20140810/giroud-on-his-community-shield-goal |first=Chris |last=Harris |publisher=Arsenal Football Club |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref>

[[File:Community Shield 60 - Celebrations (14698442567).jpg|thumb|left|upright=1.25|The Arsenal players celebrating their win]] 
Pellegrini was not overly concerned by Manchester City's defeat and said: "The season starts next Sunday," referring to their league campaign.<ref name="pell">{{cite news |title=Manchester City: Manuel Pellegrini confident of Premier League title |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28734488 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref> He admitted Arsenal had played the better football in the first half, but felt his team were much improved in the second – "we had possession and chances to score but we didn't."<ref name="pell"/> Pellegrini felt the absence of several Manchester City players had a bearing on the result and said he planned to talk to the players to get them ready for the season ahead. Of Caballero's inclusion ahead of [[Joe Hart]], the manager said: "That was one game more for the pre-season."<ref>{{cite news |title=Manuel Pellegrini admits Manchester City are not ready for Premier League season after Arsenal defeat |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/manuel-pellegrini-admits-manchester-city-4033844|first=James |last=Nursey |newspaper=Daily Mirror |location=London |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref> City's stand-in captain Touré, like his manager, was not despondent about the result; he described playing Arsenal as a "good test" for the team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Yaya Touré reaction |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/citytv/Interviews/2014/August/Arsenal-v-City-Community-Shield-Yaya-reaction |website=mcfc.co.uk |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014 |archive-date=14 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814000108/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/citytv/Interviews/2014/August/Arsenal-v-City-Community-Shield-Yaya-reaction |url-status=dead }}</ref>

FA General Secretary Alex Horne hinted afterwards that the Community Shield could be played overseas, though not any time before 2018 because of the existing contract with Wembley Stadium. He described it as an interesting idea and told reporters: "The [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] are doing it and we know that Spanish football<!--Not true, but this is a quote--> and Italian football are looking at doing that with their own Supercup-type games."<ref>{{cite news |title=FA confirms Community Shield's future may be overseas |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/news/11024967/FA-confirms-Community-Shields-future-may-be-overseas.html |first=Ben |last=Rumsby |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}}</ref>

An average of 860,000 viewers watched the match live on BT Sport, down by almost 2,000,000 on the previous year's Community Shield which was aired on [[ITV (TV channel)|ITV]]. The channel's coverage peaked at 1.2&nbsp;million viewers (8.4% of the [[Audience measurement|audience share]]) during the second half.<ref>{{cite news|title=The Village returns with 4.6m |url=http://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/ratings/the-village-returns-with-46m/5076111.article?blocktitle=Ratings&contentID=39826 |work=Broadcast |first=Peter |last=White |location=London |date=11 August 2014 |access-date=11 August 2014}} {{subscription required}}</ref>
